 HAZE: Art with a Purpose coming to Wellsville on November 29
 Share: 
 Meet the artist Hazel Freeman who invites you to the Wellsville American Legion
 By Andrew Harris
 A Wellsville 9th grader has discovered her power in art and she’s ready to share her early work with the community later this month. Hazel Freeman and her family will host a special premier show on Sunday November 29th from 11am until 2pm that everyone is invited to attend. 
 It won’t just be an art show because that is only half of Hazel’s story. This art has been made with and through years of pain and frustration, and the love and support of family and friends. Hazel has Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) and almost immediately upon her diagnosis became an advocate for others facing the condition. The Freeman’s invite you to stop by, check out Hazel’s work, talk about her journey to this point, and perhaps buy some original work. 
 This premier show could be historic… this young lady could be the next Georgia O’Keeffe or Hilma af Klint!!
 We got a chance to ask Hazel a few questions about her art, her mission, and what to expect on the 29th:
 When did your love for creating art start and when did you realize you had this special talent ? 
 Hazel: When my dad showed me his sketchbook for the first time, and I loved it.
 Your mom Megan has always been very artistic. How has she influenced you ? 
 Hazel: Honestly, it was both of my parents. I remember my dad would show me his sketchbook from when he was younger, and I thought it was so good. My mom always influenced me with design and photography, but I definitely got my dad’s drawing talents.
 Have you had an art teacher or fellow artist that needs a shout out? Explain why? 
 Hazel: My aunt (Mrs. McNulty) — I have always found her style really interesting.
 This show will shine a light on Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) which you face daily. Explain how you are using art to advocate for yourself and others ? 
 Hazel: Honestly, I find that I use art for more of my emotions like anger and sadness, but painting definitely distracts myself from the pain. I’m really happy to be advocating for CRPS so people are more aware.
 What is the one piece in this show that is a must-see, don’t-miss-it work of art ? 
 Hazel: THE PILL. I made that one the time we got out of Cleveland Clinic and we took off SO MANY MEDS. At that point, I was taking so many it just felt like a meal.
 Hazels big sis Maddie, an artist as well, noticed her siblings talent very early in life, 
 “Haze has always been an artist — even at 3 she was coloring inside the lines. But over the years, her art has gotten more in depth, more personal, and sometimes i can’t even believe that a 14 year old made that. I love watching my sister excel at something she’s so passionate in.” 
 Hazel’s mother Megan Freeman also say a special talent early on, “We’ve been impressed with Hazel’s artwork since she was little. I think the first time we really recognized her artistic talent was when she poked a hole into a plastic water bottle and drew a face on our garage floor by squirting the water out. We are amazed at what she’s been able to create.”
 By Hazel Freeman, 2021 at age 9 
 From Dad, Nick Freeman: Haze – We love you and are so proud of you for everything you have accomplished. We know it hasn’t been easy but we will always be here to support you, and can’t wait to see what you do next. 
 Nick, Megan, and Maddie hope to see you there!! 
 “We truly can’t wait for people to see the things she’s created and we hope that everyone can come out and support!” 
 More about Hazel and the show: 
 Hazel Freeman is 14 years old and has been creating art for as long as she can remember. She lives with Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), a chronic neurological pain condition that affects her every day.
 Art is her outlet, her therapy, and her way of turning pain into something beautiful.
 Join us to enjoy Hazel’s original artwork, prints, and more while raising awareness for CRPS. Together, we hope to bring more understanding to an often invisible condition and remind others living with chronic pain that they are not alone
